t: Frederick took Silesia from Austria in the 1740s and kept it through the Seven Years' War against a coalition of Austria, France, Russia, Sweden and the Holy Roman Empire, at a heavy cost in lives and money.

He called the sovereign the first servant of the state, reformed the courts and civil service, curbed judicial torture and invited settlers of any faith, while keeping Protestantism favoured and Jews and Catholics under limits.

In 1772 he annexed most of Royal Prussia in the First Partition of Poland and set out to Germanise its people, a side of his rule that sits beside his reputation as a patron of music, letters and science.
dyk: Frederick composed 121 sonatas for flute and continuo, and visitors to his grave at Sanssouci often leave potatoes on the stone in honour of his promotion of the crop in Prussia.
ev: Frederick's attempt to flee to Britain fails, and he is forced to watch the beheading of his friend Hans Hermann von Katte at Küstrin
Frederick becomes king and invades Silesia, beginning the First Silesian War
The Treaty of Dresden confirms Prussia's hold on Silesia, and Frederick is first called 'the Great'
Frederick invades Saxony, starting the Third Silesian War and the wider Seven Years' War
Austrian and Russian forces rout Frederick's army at the Battle of Kunersdorf
The Treaty of Hubertusburg ends the war, and Prussia keeps Silesia
Frederick annexes most of Royal Prussia in the First Partition of Poland and takes the title King of Prussia
Frederick dies at Sanssouci and is succeeded by his nephew Frederick William II

f.born: 24 January 1712, in the Berlin Palace; son of Crown Prince Frederick William of Prussia and Sophia Dorothea of Hanover, of the House of Hohenzollern
f.died: 17 August 1786, in an armchair in his study at Sanssouci, Potsdam, aged 74; childless
f.role: Crown prince from 1713; King in Prussia from 1740; King of Prussia from 1772 until his death in 1786
f.known: the conquest of Silesia; the Seven Years' War; the First Partition of Poland; enlightened absolutism and the ruler as 'first servant of the state'; reform of the army, courts and civil service; flute music and patronage of the arts; Sanssouci
